title: Southampton Bounce Back as Larin Returns and Mubama Seals Derby Win
body:
They beat Derby 2-0 [S1], stretching their unbeaten home run in the Championship to 18 games [S1][S2].

The main talking point was Cyle Larin, who came back from a hamstring problem and a long goal drought to score his eighth goal of the season, his first since 12 September [S1]. Divin Mubama added a second in stoppage time [S1]. Derby are second from bottom [S1][S2], which makes the win look straightforward on paper. Saints had already dropped points against Watford, Preston, Wrexham, Lincoln and Bolton this season [S1], so the worry about weaker opponents was real and this result answers it only in part.

Elsewhere, Norwich made it five wins in a row with a 2-1 victory over Cardiff [S1]. QPR also picked up their first away win since August, beating 10-man Millwall on the road [S1]. Those results raise the stakes for the sides chasing places near the top, and they make every dropped point at home more costly.

Here is the uncomfortable truth. A long home record is pleasant to shout about, but it counts for little if the side keeps leaking points against teams they should beat. The manager will know that a comfortable home scoreline does not erase the nervousness of the last few months. The real test is whether this performance becomes a habit rather than a relief.

The Touchline Take: One to keep an eye on, because the next few results against lower-placed opponents will say far more than this one did.

evidence.text: The Guardian: Championship roundup: Southampton get Larin lift as Norwich win five in a row. Southampton 2-0 Derby; Norwich 2-1 Cardiff. QPR get first away win since August at 10-man Millwall. Cyle Larin returned to action with a bang as Southampton extended their unbeaten run at home in the Championship to 18 games with a 2-0 victory over second-bottom Derby . Larin turned in his eighth goal of the season but his first since 12 September – after a four-game drought and a hamstring problem. Divin Mubama added a second in stoppage time as Saints shrugged off worries of failing against lower-placed sides – having dropped points against Watford, Preston, Wrexham, Lincoln and Bolton already this season.
